  • Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to cling onto his Fifa presidency heading into next year’s election after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support.
  • England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to cling onto his Fifa presidency heading into next year’s election after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support.

England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027.

But as the dust has settled on his privatisation ploy, Infantino’s bid for a third term has strengthened. His allies have surfaced, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf, the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president, and now the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has reversed its position and backed Infantino with AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa underlining that there is “a true understanding between us”.

It has been revealed that infantino does have his challengers, with French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima joining the race. The deadline to submit presidential bids passed on 18 November.

But Infantino, confident of staying on for a fourth term, laughed in response to a question over whether he had considered resigning as president, declaring he retains the support of the “vast, vast majority” of world football.

Recent findings suggest that infantino needs 106 votes from the 211 member associations to be re-elected as president. Here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino:.

Recent findings suggest that uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership. They threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions before Infantino’s eventual climbdown but has continued to assert that his position is untenable, even taking legal action against the Swiss-Italian.

The body points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”.

Sources indicate that uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis has written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom setting out a series of questions on behalf of European members of the Fifa Council, demanding documents covering a series of Infantino controversies. Fifa has until 2 November to answer these questions.

Concacaf, the Confederation for North America and the Caribbean, came out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject.

After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.”.

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani was initially seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election but he now looks set to pursue another term as Concacaf chief.

The Albanian Football Federation aligned itself with Uefa.

“The Albanian Football Association has sent an official letter to Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafström, informing him that it has withdrawn its support for Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for another four-year term as Fifa President,” the statement confirmed.

Rinse and repeat for Austria’s federation, who said “a united approach by the European associations sends a strong signal of responsibility for the sport and of solidarity.”.

Recent findings suggest that belgium, who felt the brunt of another Infantino controversy at the World Cup over Folarin Balogun’s red card, have withdrawn their support for his re-election. citing Fifa’s failure to demonstrate “any transparency” under his leadership.

As did the Croatian Football Federation (HNS): "The Croatian Football Federation has informed Fifa of its decision to withdraw the support previously expressed for Mr Gianni Infantino's candidature for another term as Fifa president.

In a recent development, "This decision followed a thorough reassessment within the federation in light of recent developments surrounding the Fifa World Cup 2026 and discussions within our governing bodies. We consider our position to be clearly communicated to Fifa and have no further comment to add at this time.".

The Cyprus Football Association (CFA) aligned itself with Uefa’s position and remarked it felt Infantino could no longer continue as president.

"Under the weight of what has taken place and under today's conditions, the CFA finds that the necessary prerequisites are no longer in place for the President of Fifa to continue exercising his duties," the association stated.

Denmark did not endorse Infantino’s re-election bid prior to the scheme’s reveal and haven’t changed their stance.

It has been revealed that there is also a precedent for their opposition to Infantino, with federation president Jesper Moller not supporting his re-election efforts back in 2022: “There is only one candidate ... but Denmark will not be supporting the current president.”.

The English FA is one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027.

Infantino’s apology letter changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme.

Sources indicate that all the Nordic nations ended up joining forces in a combined statement, to say they had “lost confidence” in Infantino’s leadership. This included the Faroe Islands.

Finland kickstarted the process of formal withdrawals, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino.

France withdrew their endorsement of Infantino in September and proposed to seek ways to transform how Fifa is run.

"A project with such a significant impact on the future of football could not be envisaged without comprehensive information, in-depth consultation and a fully transparent decision-making process," FFF president Philippe Diallo said in a statement, who is now running against Infantino as Uefa’s last-minute candidate. "Fifa's governance does not live up to the standards that football represents.".

The Georgian Football Federation similarly withdrew its support for Infantino’s candidacy.

The German federation (DFB) already opted against endorsing Infantino earlier in the year so has not had to send a letter withdrawing support to take an opposing stance.

Sources indicate that “The DFB has not signed a letter of support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino," the governing body stated in July. "Further steps will be discussed in the DFB presidential board.".

Former Germany national team director Oliver Bierhoff further reiterated the nation’s loss of trust in Infantino: "We have to take care of football. It is already commercial but it is a property for all of football. The world views may be different but in the last weeks and months a lot happened so that we have no trust any more that it will be going in the right direction.".

Another smaller footballing nation to withdraw its endorsement, Gibraltar aligned itself with Uefa.

“Accordingly, the Gibraltar FA has decided that it can no longer maintain its endorsement of Mr Infantino’s candidature for the 2027 Fifa presidential election. Fifa has been formally informed of that decision,” a statement read.

The Greek Football Association has backed Uefa’s push for a change in Fifa’s leadership, similarly withdrawing support to underscore a united European front in opposition to Infantino.

"The Greek FA (EPO) has taken a clear position against a candidacy of Gianni Infantino," EPO presdient Makis Gagatsis told reporters. "We saw things happen at the World Cup that are not acceptable to football public opinion. Then... came a programme to sell World Cup rights and we are clearly against it, so we withdrew our support of the Fifa president.".

Part of the Nordic collective against the incumbent president, Iceland have also lost confidence in Infantino.

The Israel Football Association was another to formally send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its endorsement of Infantino’s re-election.

In his letter, FA president Moshe Zuares claims there was an “unprecedented crisis of confidence” between the visions of Uefa and Fifa when it comes to global governance, adding that the rift is “profound, substantive, and principled, and compelling all stakeholders to reconsider the path forward”.

The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) initially delayed taking official action but it has now withdrawn its support for Infantino's candidacy in the next Fifa presidential election scheduled.

"This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC's position - in full agreement with Uefa and its president Aleksander Ceferin - regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions," FIGC said in a statement.

The Football Association of Montenegro has withdrawn its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid for another term.

“The proposals that have been put forward, as they assessed, have exposed worrying vulnerabilities in terms of governance, not only at the political level but also within the administration,” a statement read. “Therefore, the Football Association of Montenegro has decided to withdraw its letter of support, previously given in favour of Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for re-election in 2027.”.

The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) is among the many to have confirmed it has lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

Sources indicate that “The way this process has unfolded has resulted in a fundamental loss of confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino. The KNVB no longer has confidence in his leadership,” a statement read.

The Northern Irish football association (IFA) has expressed “concerns” over Infantino’s leadership.

Sources indicate that "We take our responsibilities as a member association of both Uefa and Fifa seriously," stated an IFA spokesperson. "We support the current Uefa position on the matter and will continue to engage constructively on complications relating to football governance. We are of course aware of the recent developments and wider concerns within the football community. We are considering these matters carefully and will continue to engage through the appropriate governance structures and channels.”.

The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) have been one of the most vocal bodies to call for Infantino’s resignation.

NFF president Lise Klaveness told the Guardian: “We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now. We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

Sources indicate that “We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has followed in withdrawing its support for Infantino while backing Uefa’s stance.

According to recent reports, "Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," it confirmed. "It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning. The Association is grateful for the support that Fifa provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.”.

The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) was among the countries to resolutely reject the sell-off proposal, calling it “a dangerous initiative to turn football into a private asset”.

As a result, the FRF will withhold support for Infantino’s re-election for the time being, with a statement reading: “FRF is suspending the discussion regarding the support of Fifa President Gianni Infantino for a latest term, until further clarifications.”.

The SFA’s chief executive Ian Maxwell told the BBC that the governing body’s position has “been clear” since Uefa’s collective statement.

He stated: “We have aligned ourselves with the Uefa position and 55 nations are stronger than one voice. Their statement since then has talked about a lack of confidence in the Fifa leadership and the Scottish FA agree completely with that decision. The SFA will not be voting for Gianni Infantino come the re-election in early 2027.”.

The Football Association of Serbia sent a similar letter withdrawing support to Fifa.

“We would like to remind you that we provided our support to Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May of this year, but after carefully considering the events that have seriously damaged the image and reputation of both Fifa and its president in the past period, this is the only logical and rational course of action,” a statement read.

Sweden’s federation (SvFF) followed suit: "At an extraordinary board meeting on Monday, SvFF has chosen not to support Fifa President Gianni Infantino ​in the upcoming re-election.

"This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. The decision is based on recurring shortcomings in governance, transparency and management, which means that trust in Gianni Infantino's leadership no longer exists.".

The Swiss Football Association (SFV) withdrew its backing of Infantino’s bid for another term as Fifa president at the end of September, saying it “cannot justify continuing to support Gianni Infantino’s candidacy”.

Their former international captain Ramon Vega unveiled he would be challenging Infantino but was not included on the final list of candidates published by Fifa.

The Football Association of Wales was one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino.

Sources indicate that “The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”.

The United States joined forces with Canada to call for “meaningful change that strengthens Fifa’s governance, transparency and accountability”.

Same as above, with Canadian prime minister Mark Carney stating that he no longer has confidence in Infantino.

“It should be fatal,” Carney mentioned following Infantino’s botched sell-off plan. “Certainly I don’t have confidence in Mr. Infantino.".

The Japanese Football Federation (JFA) are backing their own candidate for president, with Kozo Tashima challenging Infantino. This signifies a rupture in Asia’s collective backing of Infantino, with Tashima confirming he already has at least five member associations backing him on the continent.

Asked about his ‌objectives, the 68-year-old Tashima mentioned: "First and foremost, I believe it is essential to establish proper governance and ensure that transparency is firmly maintained.

It has been revealed that "We must get that right first. Then, on top of that, various policies can be put forward.".

Jordan were the first non-Uefa member association to publicly oppose Infantino after federation president Prince Ali bin Hussein levelled accusations of blackmail against Fifa.

Prince Ali alleged the organisation offered assistance with the kingdom's concerns in exchange for his endorsement, following Infantino's withdrawal from a World Cup stake sale proposal. Among the problems cited was the association's eight-month wait for prize money, due since December for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

After taking to X to reveal the outstanding payments, the Jordan Football Association received the prize money two days later - but Prince Ali has not changed his stance over not endorsing Infantino: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”.

New Zealand have broken rank with Oceania’s confederation by withdrawing their support for Infantino.

"After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within Fifa have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust,” a statement read.

Confederation of African Football (54 members) 🌍.

Caf, the governing body for African football, was the first confederation to unanimously back Infantino.

“We are committed to continue working together with Fifa, its member associations, other football confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency global best practises and to contribute to the development and growth of football worldwide,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said.

Motsepe later added that the position of embattled president Infantino can only be decided by Fifa elections.

Asian Football Confederation (47 members) 🌏.

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has endorsed Infantino in an apparent turnaround in its stance from two months ago when it criticised the head of football’s world governing body for a breach of trust.

AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, speaking at the body’s extraordinary congress meeting in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement.

“We affirm our full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a latest mandate as the Fifa president.” Sheikh Salman said. “You’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well.”.

South American governing body Conmebol, with its 10 member associations, expressed “concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken” and welcomed the decision to withdraw the plans, affirming it will “not support any action” that “ignores or deviates” from the “democratic procedures that represent the 211 Fifa member associations”.

But having already endorsed Infantino in the summer, they have now stuck with their stance and not wavered as one of the Swiss-Italian’s firmest strongholds, something which was confirmed as the 10 member associations met in November.

“This serves as recognition of the leadership of the current FIFA president and the positive transformations within football,” Conmbeol remarked in a statement.

Caribbean Football Union (25 members) 🌎.

In a recent development, following a pair of visits to the Caribbean, the CFU revealed on Friday that it will endorse Infantino for another term. This is despite Concacaf, the governing body of North America and the Caribbean, being in opposition.

“The CFU emphasizes that it determined its collective position through consultation with its member associations,” the organisation stated in a statement. “In this same spirit the CFU continues to call for increased transparency, good governance, and meaningful reform within the football family.”.

Uefa is not fully unified in its opposition of Infantino, with Azerbaijan one of two nations to publicly back the incumbent president.

“The Association of Football Federations of Azerbaijan (AFFA) fully supports Fifa and Fifa President Gianni Infantino,” a statement read after a visit to Hovsan.

Similarly, the association of Latvia has stood in support of Infantino amid criticism from Uefa.

“Gianni Infantino does so many things that it is difficult to list in one minute, but I am grateful for his support around the world, his contribution to the development of football, and, of course, Latvia is always on his side,” stated federation president Vadims Lyashenko. “He can count on our support.”.

Benin’s federation looks set to back Infantino in next March’s election.

“I see no reason not to support him,” remarked Mathurin de Chacus, president of the Benin federation.

FA president Alexandre Muyenge of Burundi echoed the remarks by his Benin counterpart supporting Infantino.

He noted: “He is a president who is doing what is necessary to support Africa, particularly the less wealthy countries. His record is good, so it is logical to support him.".

The president of the Comoros Football Federation, Noted Ali Athouman, backed Infantino’s scheme due to the financial benefits to smaller nations.

Sources indicate that "Our problem is how to obtain money,” he stated. “Right now, we have no sponsors. So how do we compete? The richest nations can train players, have infrastructure and equipment, and it's no coincidence that they then achieve results. Most European countries don't have ​these problems.”.

The Djiboutian Football Federation has similarly welcomed the decision to withdraw the sell-off proposal, with president Souleiman Hassan Waberi saying the climbdown “demonstrates a firm commitment to preserving the unity, solidarity and cohesion that define the football family”.

He remarked in a statement: “I reaffirm my full support for Fifa President Mr Gianni Infantino and for all initiatives aimed at promoting the sustainable, transparent and inclusive development of football around the world.”.

Recent findings suggest that DR Congo's federation (Fecofa) president Veron Mosengo-Omba, who was only elected in May, spoke out in “full support” of Infantino. The two studied at university in Switzerland together.

Fecofa said it had "greatly benefited" from Fifa's programmes, citing investment in development and infrastructure.

Egypt have maintained their endorsement of Infantino, similar to heir North African counterparts.

"The Egyptian Football Association reiterates its full trust in President Gianni Infantino's leadership and its continuous support for any initiatives that benefit Fifa member associations and the future of world football,” a statement read.

Lamin Kaba Bajo told BBC Sport that his federation not just stood by Infantino, but would do "everything within our means" to get him re-elected.

"That's my personal opinion as president of the federation, and a good number of African memberships also stand on that line. He is here to stay,” he said.

Fleetwood Haiya, Malawi's football chief, cited the nation’s financial concerns in why he supported Infantino.

In a recent development, he told BBC Sport: "Our government is not able to make sure that they have medical supplies in hospitals and at the same time to look at football. Malawi needs money.".

Ahmed Yahya, the country's representative on the Fifa Council, was one of a number of African football leaders to say he was backing Infantino early on, pledging his support before Caf took its stance.

The location of Infantino’s initial crisis meeting back in the summer, Morocco have stuck by the Swiss-Italian as one of his most loyal allies.

“What has been achieved in recent years through Fifa’s development programmes, particularly in Africa, represents an key accomplishment that must be preserved, to the benefit of all member associations,” said the Royal Moroccan Football Federation’s president Fouzi Lekjaa.

Like Mauritania, Hamidou Djibrilla from Niger came out swiftly in support of Infantino.

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has largely aligned itself towards a supportive stance for Infantino's leadership, with former NFF president and deputy chairman of Fifa's Men's National Teams Competitions Committee, Amaju Pinnick, backing his initial sell-off blueprint.

Namibia Football Association president Robert Shimooshili has backed Infantino and reiterated that his federation stands with Caf.

Sources indicate that “If CAF rallies behind Infantino, then we also support the president of Fifa at the moment. We have confidence in him, and we don’t mind what Uefa or AFC or Concacaf say. That is their right and we cannot do anything about it,” he noted.

Sudan’s federation joined five other Arab nations - Qatar, Lebanon, Morocco, Egypt and Mauritania - in writing a joint statement backing Infantino.

Recent findings suggest that "Recognising the important role of Arab football in bringing people together and strengthening co-operation among football associations across the Arab world, we ... express our full support for Mr Gianni Infantino, president of Fifa, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide," the statement read.

Industry observers note that "We deeply appreciate Mr Infantino’s sustained efforts to advance football globally, expand opportunities across all regions and strengthen the game’s role in bringing people and communities together. We look forward to continuing our close cooperation with him towards a stronger and more prosperous future for world ‌football, expanding opportunities and further enhancing Arab football’s contribution to ​the global game.".

While not an official statement from the federation, South Africa’s Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture of South Africa, Gayton McKenzie, posted on X saying that Infantino had been "very good to African football".

Recent findings suggest that "Africa should be cautious in joining the public lynching of Infantino,” he warned. “He has been very good to African football. We can debate his ideas but let's not forget who has been a friend to us. Many of those calling for his head want the old status quo back too.".

The Ugandan federation are said to have echoed the sentiments of Malawi and comoros, with football officials from the federation telling BBC Sport that Fifa investment has transformed their game both on and off the pitch.

The Bhutan Football Federation has published a letter that extends its “sincere appreciation” to Infantino for scrapping the aims, hailing him for demonstrating “true leadership” by “prioritising consensus over commerce”.

“We stand united with Fifa and President Infantino in their ongoing efforts to serve the global football community,” wrote federation president Dasho Ugen Tsechup.

Like others, Kuwait welcomed the decision to halt the plans but Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Al-Sabah, the president of the Kuwait Football Association, affirmed his support for Infantino.

A statement read: “He concluded by affirming the Kuwait Football Association's confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino, and its support for efforts aimed at developing the game and enhancing its opportunities for growth in a way that serves all national associations and achieves the shared interests of global football.”.

Lebanon, who granted Infantino citizenship last year, have backed the Swiss-Italian, with FA president Hashim Haidar all but echoing the same sentiments as Kuwait.

In a recent development, “Haidar reaffirms the Lebanese Football Association’s support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and his confidence in the decisions he makes in the best interests of global football, as well as in his efforts and initiatives aimed at developing the game,” he stated, while also asserting that Infantino’s proposal “could be re-examined ... in a away that serves the greater good of the sport and preserves its unity”.

The president of the Indonesian FA supported Infantino’s sell-off blueprint and has now backed him for another term.

Hailing Fifa as a “strategic partner that is truly present” in its football development, Erick Thohir said: “This is proof of President Infantino’s vision that football development must not be centered on a single region; it must proceed worldwide.”.

The Mongolian Football Federation has likewise put out a statement in support of Infantino.

Qatar was the first football association to publicly back Infantino during his attempts to sell off the World Cup, even though they later welcomed the decision to scrap the blueprint.

In a recent development, "While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among member associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally,” a statement read.

Philippines have also backed Infantino and called for co-operation among confederations.

"We stand behind President Gianni Infantino's leadership, and trust that continued dialogue among all confederations and member associations will keep the global game moving forward together,” the Philippines confirmed.

Saudi Arabia, the controversial host of the 2034 World Cup, unsurprisingly came out in support of Infantino in the fallout of the scandal.

"At this time, SAFF supports the continued efforts ​of Fifa President Gianni Infantino and Fifa’s leadership to restore unity across ⁠the football family and continue growing the game for the benefit of all," ​the federation mentioned in a statement on its website.

Like Qatar, Sri Lanka welcomed the decision to scrap the investment strategy and has since reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

Industry observers note that "One of President Infantino's defining leadership qualities has always been his willingness to listen to the views and concerns of Member Associations. This decision is a clear reflection of his inclusive leadership style, built on dialogue, mutual respect, and a genuine commitment to serving the global football community," its statement read.

The UAE Football Association backed Infantino after Fifa withdrew its proposed private investment initiative, with president Sheikh Hamdan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan saying the FA “reaffirmed its confidence” in his leadership.

Argentina became the first member from South America to voice its support for Infantino, on the same day that confederation Conmebol - which had previously only expressed backing of Infantino - expressed concern over Fifa’s procedures.

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the Fifa board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent,” a statement read.

The Ecuador federation (FEF) welcomed the proposal’s withdrawal and expressed confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

“We trust that you, and those who are presently leading football, will continue working for the benefit of our sport,” read the statement.

Paraguay also followed suit as Infantino’s Conmebol support base surfaced.

Their federation published a letter of support addressed to Infantino, writing that it "reaffirms its commitment to continue working alongside Fifa”.

Venezuela was another from South America to publicly support Infantino.

“We reiterate our commitment to continue working shoulder to shoulder under your leadership and with the other sister associations to promote the massification and excellence of all modalities of our discipline,” read a statement from the federation.

One of the many island nations to break away from Concacaf is Antigua and Barbuda, with the Caribbean being re-established as an Infantino stronghold.

“[Infantino’s] transformative policies, from ground-breaking investment in grassroots infrastructure to the historic expansion of World Cup access, have elevated the aspirations of emerging football nations into attainable realities,” the ABFA mentioned in a statement. “By listening with genuine humility and acting with decisive conviction, he has forged a legacy of inclusivity that transcends the sport itself, affirming that every nation, regardless of size, deserves equal voice and fair opportunity on the world stage.”.

Another Caribbean federation to support Infantino’s leadership is the British Virgin Islands.

BVI FA president Avanell Morton remarked: “Well, what more can he do? He’s doing a fantastic job already and doing a fantastic job for the entire region. It’s about football and as long as you are about football, then you have the opportunity to make football the priority.”.

Grenada’s federation (GFA) has also broken away from the Concacaf block and reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

“The GFA reaffirms its support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and expresses its sincere appreciation for his continued support for football development in Grenada and across the Caribbean over his period of service in office and for the years to come,” a statement read.

JFF president Michael Ricketts has similarly reaffirmed his federation’s support in Infantino, breaking away from the Concacaf stance.

“I think Infantino has done so very well for football globally,” he said. “I remember when I got into football as the president, the support from Fifa was medial to say the least.It has been a lot better now and we are just very grateful and we are looking forward to further improvements so that we can impact not just football but the social well-being of every boy and girl who plays the sport.”.

Mexico is the only non-Caribbean Concacaf member to support Infantino, breaking away from the stance taken by its 2026 World Cup co-hosts, the United States and Canada.

Industry observers note that the Mexican Football Federation (FMF) stated: "The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made... by President Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations.".

The Saint Kitts and Nevis Football Association (SKNFA) has welcomed Infantino’s decision to scrap the proposal, called for respect of Fifa’s institutional processes and backed the president to continue.

It mentioned: “The SKNFA concluded by reaffirming its support for Infantino’s leadership and vision, and said it looks forward to supporting him as he completes his current constitutional mandate and continues efforts to advance football development across Fifa’s 211 Member Associations.”.

One of just three Caribbean nations to ever qualify for a World Cup, Trinidad and Tobago president Kieron Edwards states he has no doubts that the TTFA will back Infantino next year.

According to recent reports, “We would have given President Infantino our full support and we have not wavered with that. Things do come up, changes, you have to have discussions, you have to have dialogue but the support is there 100 per cent behind the President always,” he remarked.

With the Oceania Football Confederation yet to take an official stance, the Football Federation of American Samoa to come out on their own and back Infantino, sending a letter to the incumbent president to express “sincere gratitude for your outstanding leadership of the the Fifa family worldwide”.

New Caledonia federation president Steeve Laigle has acknowledged Infantino’s “political mistake” but continues to defend the Fifa chief, whose World Cup expansion allowed the tiny Pacific island to reach a World Cup play-off.

Papua Upcoming Guinea’s association (PNGFA) was quick to “reaffirm its full support for Fifa president Gianni Infantino” in the aftermath of his botched privatisation bid.

The Solomon Islands also expressed its “continued confidence in his leadership” in regards to Infantino’s presidency.

Tahiti are also remarked to have expressed their support before the OFC have taken an official stance.

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC), with its 11 member associations, stopped short from pulling its support for Infantino in their statement after welcoming the scrapping of the sell-off plan, very much staying on the fence as it called for a “review”.

A statement read: "The OFC recognises the progress achieved over the last decade in advancing football development in Oceania under Fifa's leadership and encourages Fifa to use the review as an opportunity to identify and implement any changes that may be necessary.".

Individual members of the confederation have already taken stances, as seen above.

As things stand, The Independent tallies that Infantino has 142 member associations backing him for re-election, while 71 members are outwardly confirmed to be opposing him. This is taking into account the endorsements of confederations, which are being considered as a blanket vote from all members under that governing body unless a member has broken rank.

For example, Jordan’s opposition to Infantino means he is not included in the other 46 AFC member associations supporting Infantino, per the confederation’s endorsement, while the likes of Mexico, Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago and more are all separate from the other Concacaf members in opposition.

Industry observers note that this suggests that Infantino is well on course for re-election. However, each nation has a vote for itself and some could go against their confederation’s stance. Japan’s decision to run a rival candidate signifies Asia is not unanimous with its support of Infantino, with Tashima having at least five other member associations backing him - something he will later reveal. Meanwhile, the Brazilian federation president publicly opposed Infantino’s sell-off plans and may not be aligned with Conmebol.

Nevertheless, there will need to be a massive swing from within Infantino’s strongholds if the tide is to turn against the Swiss-Italian come next March’s election.

Published: 01:43 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 01:45 EST, 22 November 2026.

All eyes will be on Manchester United's fresh head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

Industry observers note that liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they currently sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that united have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday.

United right now sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season.

Goalkeeper – Alisson Becker (Liverpool).

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

The 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

Right back – Ronald Araujo (Liverpool).

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

Sources indicate that the 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

In a recent development, the Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona.

Centre back - Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool).

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

It has been revealed that the 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool).

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

The team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a big decision to make.

Left back – Kostas Tsimikas (Liverpool).

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

Recent findings suggest that but across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

According to recent reports, manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular issue since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace.

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool).

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a latest five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating major chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four big chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United).

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

It has been revealed that the 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

It has been revealed that A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend.

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool).

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an important role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United).

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a substantial chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again.

Centre-forward – Alexander Isak (Liverpool).

EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

💡 Key Takeaways
  • European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.
  • When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.
  • The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.

When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.

The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

The pair then hot-footed their way to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelekenskyy.

Zelenskyy and Kushner also said Thursday that Europeans would be at the table for the next talks with Russia on ending the war.

According to recent reports, kallas is one of the figures tipped as most likely to represent the EU in any future talks to end Russia's war against Ukraine, alongside EU Council President Antonio Costa. As yet, the EU hasn’t been able to land on one central figure to send ― many of the national leaders want to be present themselves.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted Europe will be present.

"At the table must be sitting Ukraine, must be sitting the Europeans, must be sitting the Americans, and naturally Russia," he told reporters in Dublin.

But he, like many other leaders, played down the idea of appointing a special envoy for the talks.

Zelenskyy is insistent on European involvement in the peace talks.

Recent findings suggest that "Not directly yet, and not yet when the Russians are at the table," he told the other leaders during the Dublin meetings. "But Europeans are already involved. And we need to make sure that Europe becomes a regular part of these negotiations.".

Sources indicate that europe’s division over exactly who should be present has caused a public battle to erupt. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote an excoriating letter to Costa last week, bemoaning the lack of unity.

"By projecting the image of a Europe that is in disarray, we are merely serving the interests of those who want this war to continue," wrote Meloni.

European leaders had even seemed divided over their level of frustration about the situation.

Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Jansa said in Dublin that it was creating a "bad mood" among leaders, however Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs disputed those comments saying, "I don’t feel that.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The palpable fear among the leaders in Dublin is that the US will accept Russia's demands that Europe changes the way it structures its own security, mainly through the NATO military alliance, in exchange for a seat at the table.

Putin said a commitment that Ukraine will never join NATO and even the potential rolling back of the alliance to remove newly introduced joiners Finland and Sweden, could be among his demands.

According to recent reports, "What do we hear from them [Europeans]?" asked Putin during the meeting with Kushner and Witkoff in Moscow. "That once a peace agreement is signed, they will immediately deploy troops in Ukraine. This is a legitimate target for us, so the war will resume immediately.".

This is exactly the kind of rhetoric the European leaders say they are most wary of, especially those in Russia’s direct neighborhood.

"Right now, we are in the [Russian] trap," stated Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal. "If something is a threat to you, will you discuss your defense with the threat [itself]?".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump mentioned publicly that he was hoping for a "very significant, beautiful agreement" that "might involve all of Europe.".

Zelensky said he found the US approach "a bit strange.".

Many of Europe's leaders speaking in Dublin referenced previous agreements with Russia that they believe Moscow has breached.

They include the 1975 Helsinki Accords, the 1990 Paris Charter, 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act and the one they consider most notable: the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which forbids Russia from using force against Ukraine unless in self-defense.

The rancor over the seat at the peace talks is drawing focus away from arguably the bigger battle in the EU now ― how to fund Ukraine as the war continues.

Back in October, the European Commission identified a €70 billion hole in the EU’s funding it had promised for Ukraine’s economy.

Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico has opposed any further financial and military support for Ukraine.

But Germany's Merz warned he could block the EU's next seven-year budget unless member states agree to contribute to Ukraine's financing.

One day it will have to end for Harry Kane, but for now, almost 12 years into his England life, there is still no matching the wisdom and influence he has accumulated over all those games and all those goals for his country.

In a recent development, this would have been a great night by any measure for a man collecting his record-breaking 126th England cap. There was a handshake from Peter Shilton, now deposed as king of caps, and a flourish by Kane of his recently acquired Ballon d’Or, once his four children had accompanied him on to the pitch. These are the nights of which dreams are made, and yet – given the defining feature of Kane’s career – there was one more thing to accomplish.

According to recent reports, that was a goal from the man who has ploughed relentlessly past the two great England individual landmarks of caps and goals. His second-half penalty won the game and, although he is not infallible from the spot, he is as close to that status as England have ever had. Age has not yet run him down, he can still bend the game to his will, and when it comes to the pressure moments, his longevity seems to offer the upper hand.

This was always going to be Kane’s night, with a great banner on the west side of the stadium paying tribute to the England captain. The Prince of Wales was in attendance for the occasion, too. Luka Modric presented his former Tottenham Hotspur team-mate with a keepsake from the Croatian football federation. Kane had to wait for the second half for the most valuable offering of all.

After the hour, the Danish referee Morten Krogh was advised by his VAR Bastian Dankert to take a second look at a corner tangle involving Jarell Quansah, and decided to award the second-half penalty from which Kane scored. It was certainly clumsy, but these grapples have been overlooked by referees in the past. The 27th successfully converted penalty of the Kane England era followed, and the man himself played the full game.

“I think I maybe underappreciated how massive it was going to be, how big the reaction was going to be,” he told the BBC.

“I think the actual moment when Ronaldo said my name, it’s strange, it’s almost like a movie.

“In the moment, it was like in slow motion and the confetti was supposed to fall and all this, but when I watched it back, I had my hand to my mouth and maybe a couple of seconds and I was out, but in the actual moment, it felt like I was doing it for a minute.

“It was a really unique feeling because it is different to playing a game or scoring a goal, because it is so individual, it is nothing you can kind of do.

Recent findings suggest that having just experienced one of the best nights of his footballing life, Adam Wharton was not in the mood to dwell on a negative. Fresh from starring in Crystal Palace’s 1-0 victory over Rayo Vallecano in the Conference League final in May, Wharton was asked how he felt about missing out on England’s World Cup squad. The midfielder smiled, shrugged and shuffled in his chair before playing down his disappointment.

According to recent reports, “That's just part of football. It was never a guarantee I was going to go. I knew that,” Wharton stated. “I'm not going to sit here and cry about it… it's not the end of the world. I’m still young. Hopefully there's other tournaments and World Cups that I can go to in the future.”.

A few months on, that remains an ambition for Wharton. Right now, though, he has more pressing things to worry about.

Recent findings suggest that wharton, like Crystal Palace as a whole, has endured a poor start to the season. His omission from Thomas Tuchel's latest England squad did not raise any eyebrows. With the January window set to open in just over six weeks, Wharton's suitors must ask themselves whether this is a mere blip or a sign of deeper problems.

Industry observers note that there are mitigating factors behind his dip in form. The transition from Oliver Glasner to Pierre Sage was not smooth, culminating in the Frenchman's expected sacking. Wharton has not had a consistent partner in the engine room, with Daichi Kamada and Quentin Timber - two players with very different characteristics - taking turns alongside him.

In a recent development, when Dean Henderson was out injured earlier this season, Wharton was made captain. The armband appeared to weigh him down.

Wharton has also missed Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, Palace's two primary goal threats who have had disrupted starts to the campaign. Wharton's through-balls are most effective when they are aimed at players with the pace to run onto them. Yeremy Pino and Kamada, the wide forwards against Liverpool before the international break, are not ideal targets.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

According to recent reports, for all that, Wharton himself would be the first to admit that his performances have been far below his usual standards. His confidence has deserted him. Not helped by a collective lack of compactness out of possession, Wharton has too often been overrun. His tendency to go to ground when attempting to win the ball back carries substantial risk, leaving him out of the game if the tackle is unsuccessful.

Most worrying is his reduced effectiveness with the ball. Data from analytics manufacturer Gradient Sports reveals that only Elliot Anderson (107) and Jan Paul van Hecke (97) have attempted more line-breaking passes than Wharton, but the Palace man ranks joint-12th for line-breaking passes completed. His pass completion rate is a lowly 74%.

Industry observers note that this has always been Wharton’s game. He has never been a safe distributor, preferring instead to put the ball at risk in the hope of creating something. Of Premier League midfielders who have played more than 100 minutes this season, only Vitaly Janelt (44.8%) has a higher percentage of passes played forward than Wharton (43.6%).

According to recent reports, the trade-off was worth it for Palace last season, but when Wharton’s radar is slightly off, he becomes extremely wasteful. That raises an notable question. A Syrian who arrived in Germany as a refugee in 2015 has won a mayoral election in the southwestern German state of Baden-Württemberg.

Sources indicate that ryyan Alshebl, who left his hometown of As Suwayda in Syria eight years ago, ran as an independent in the municipality of Ostelsheim. He won 55.41% of the votes on Sunday, beating two German candidates, Marco Strauss and Mathias Fey.

Locals cheered the 29-year-old when he welcomed his win, a victory he described as “sensational,” German local broadcaster SWR reported Monday.

“Today, Ostelsheim sent an example for broad-mindedness and cosmopolitanism for the whole of Germany,” he said, according to to German public broadcaster ZDF. “That’s not something that can be taken for granted in a conservative, rural area.”.

Alshebl’s first call after his victory was to his mother in Syria, who was thrilled with the news, SWR reported.

Sources indicate that the Association of Municipalities of Baden-Württemberg said Alshebl is the first man with Syrian roots to run for and win a mayor’s office. He will start his role in June.

'You are not a refugee.' Roma refugees fleeing war in Ukraine say they are suffering discrimination and prejudice.

Ostelsheim residents have welcomed their incoming mayor. “The fairy tale has come true, and the right man has become our mayor,” Annette Keck, who lives in the village, told SWR.

Strauss, one of his opponents, congratulated Alshebl. “I wish you good luck and at the same time ask for support for Mr. Alshebl, for our shared Ostelsheim,” he mentioned on Facebook.

Recent findings suggest that the state’s Integration Minister Manne Lucha stated that Alshebl’s victory demonstrated that diversity is a natural part of Baden-Württemberg. “I would be very pleased if Ryyan Alshebl’s election encourages more people with a migration history to run for political office,” he said.

Not everyone has been so warm to the 29-year-old. ZDF reported the Syrian received hateful comments on the campaign trail.

The young politician went from house to house, promoting his election program, and “the experiences were predominantly positive,” but there was also a minority of far-right fringe voters in Ostelsheim that did not want to accept him due to his Syrian roots, Alshebl told ZDF.

Born to a schoolteacher and agricultural engineer in Syria, Alshebl described his life as carefree until the age of 20, according to his campaign website.

In a recent development, at the time, protests against the Syrian government that began in 2011 soon devolved into chaotic war. The fighting and later rise of ISIS forced 10.6 million people from home by late 2015 – about half of Syria’s pre-war population.

Alshebl faced the dilemma of being drafted for military service with the Syrian army or leaving the country, according to his website.

Industry observers note that while many Syrians were displaced internally or fled to countries in the region, others like Alshebl made the dangerous journey to Europe. He was 21 years old at the time, and noted he crossed from Turkey to the Greek island of Lesbos in a rubber dinghy.

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel had implemented a brief open-door policy in 2015 that saw the country take in about 1.2 million asylum seekers in the following years, including Alshebl.

The move sparked a backlash in Germany and the sudden growth of the far-right, anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the wake of summer 2015.

Once in Germany, Alshebl lived close to Ostelsheim and noted at the time he felt “there is only one thing you can do: get back on your feet promptly and start investing in your own future quickly.”.

For the last seven years he worked in the administration of Althengstett town hall, in a neighboring town. He drew from his experience, he mentioned in his campaign, and made digital access to to public administration services one of priorities. Flexible childcare and climate protections are also on his agenda.

Alshebl, who is a member of the Green Party and now has German citizenship, pledged during his campaign that once elected as mayor he would move to Ostelsheim.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk remains uncertain of whether he will remain at the club beyond the end of the season.

The 35-year-old centre-back is approaching the final six months of his contract, which expires next summer.

He believes that he can keep playing at the top level for “many more years” but notes he has “no idea” whether that will be at Anfield as Liverpool’s decision-makers continue to ponder over a fresh offer.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk told Sky Sports.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see. At this moment of time, if anyone claims that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the upcoming year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a massive part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

Industry observers note that "If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.".

Van Dijk has won two Premier League titles, including the club’s first in 30 years, as well as a Champions League with Liverpool, stamping his mark as one of the greatest centre-backs in the English top flight’s history since his £75m arrival from Southampton in 2018.

He is one of the last remaining figures from Jurgen Klopp’s side that won every trophy there was to win between 2019 and 2022, with Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson notably bidding emotional farewells at the end of last season.

Asked about the prospect of having to say goodbye to Anfield himself, Van Dijk stated: "Well, yeah, probably for me the most and the family because it's been an incredible time.

"But I don't look too far in the future and that's been, in my opinion, also a little bit of a success. I won't change it now either.

Sources indicate that "Whatever happens, happens. Let's see.".

Liverpool host Manchester United for new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first game on Sunday afternoon.

Why is Kai Havertz always offside for Arsenal this season?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In the Champions League final showdown with Paris Saint-Germain, Arteta again called on the German, and was duly rewarded as he fired the north London side in front with just six minutes on the clock.
  • It has been revealed that saying that, there is more to Havertz’s game than just putting the ball in the back of the net.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that injuries hardly aided Kai Havertz last season. Regardless, his standing within the Arsenal squad was evidently high. As the Gunners went in search of a first Premier League title for 22 years, he was the one who Mikel Arteta turned to during the run-in, despite Viktor Gyokeres’ major money summer arrival from Sporting CP.

In the Champions League final showdown with Paris Saint-Germain, Arteta again called on the German, and was duly rewarded as he fired the north London side in front with just six minutes on the clock. Unsurprisingly, Havertz remains the Gunners’ first-choice frontman, even if a return of three goals in the opening 10 league outings is hardly a great return.

It has been revealed that saying that, there is more to Havertz’s game than just putting the ball in the back of the net. The Germany international’s selflessness and impressive link-up play is a key reason behind his continued selection ahead of a more natural No. 9 in Gyokeres. Arteta wants his leading forward to drop deeper to bring teammates into play, dragging markers out of position to open up space for the wingers to exploit.

According to recent reports, and yet, his offside numbers resemble that of former AC Milan and Italy icon Filippo Inzaghi. “That lad must have been born offside,” Sir Alex Ferguson once quipped about the Italian, who addressed the comments to FourFourTwo back in 2023. In the modern day, Ferguson’s quote would be applicable to Havertz.

It has been revealed that after all, Havertz has been flagged offside 15 times in the Premier League this season. It’s almost double that of the player in second for this metric, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin (8) his closest competitor. He’s been penalised for being in the wrong place more times than four Premier League teams.

For context, Bukayo Saka was caught offside more times (14) than any other player in the 2025/26 Premier League campaign. Havertz did so on just three occasions. “Certainly, it’s far too many,” Arteta mentioned of the number of times Arsenal have been caught offside in the Premier League this season following the 1-0 win over Hull City prior to the international break.

So, for a player who is renowned for dropping deep in order to help his side in the final third, why has Kai Havertz been flagged offside so often this season?

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Well, for a start, Arsenal are a team that see more of the ball than the majority of the other 19 teams in England’s top tier. Only Manchester City (65.9%) and Tottenham Hotspur (63%) have managed a greater possession share than the defending champions (59.8%) in the Premier League. A return of 1379 successful final third passes is the second-most. So, too, is 31 total through balls.

It’s only natural that the amount of final third passes would result in a higher number of offsides. When teams attack an opposition backline, the side on the back foot will understandably work harder to catch you offside.

Industry observers note that who is to blame then? Obviously Havertz is at fault but he’s making the requisite runs to try and get in on goal.

According to Opta, only Fulham’s Gonzalo Garcia (145) and Manchester United forward Bryan Mbeumo (141) have made more in-behind high-intensity runs than Havertz (125) in the Premier League this season.

Despite his gangly appearance, the former Chelsea man is deceptively quick off the mark.

It has been revealed that he’s playing off the shoulder of the last defender, and if those in support were prepared to release the ball a little quicker, then his runs would be capitalised upon to great effect. However, his teammates have been guilty of taking an extra touch, or taking a split-second longer to play the pass for Havertz. As such, his momentum takes him beyond the last man, meaning he either needs to check his run late, and a chance breaks down, or stray offside.

It has been revealed that of course, as things stand, Arsenal are hardly faltering domestically as a result of Havertz’s fondness for the flag. Admittedly, though, 15 goals scored doesn’t make for great reading - it’s level with Ipswich Town. And there will come a moment where these ill-timed runs and passes do have a detrimental impact on the team. “Yes, it’s something to improve,” Arteta added following the Hull triumph. It’s an issue that he concedes requires focus.

Yet Arsenal’s relentlessness combined with a watertight backline that has shipped just five goals means they are managing to get the job done.

It has been revealed that six of their 10 league wins have been by a single goal. A little more synchronisation between Havertz and the ammo suppliers would go a long way to give Arsenal more breathing space in their title defence.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As PEN International marks Imprisoned Writer Day on November 15, a memoir by 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi stands as a powerful act of resistance against authoritarian regimes.

"A Woman Never Stops Fighting — My Struggle for Freedom, Democracy and Human Rights in Iran," was recently published in German and is set to be released in English in September 2027.

The autobiography "portrays how Narges actually became the woman she is today — and it also reveals the price she had to pay to become that woman," Mariam Claren, spokesperson for the Narges Mohammadi Foundation Germany told DW.

Mohammadi wrote the autobiography in prison: "She was constantly writing," says Claren, whose own mother, activist Nahid Taghavi, shared a cell with Mohammadi for two and a half years, in Iran's notorious Evin prison. "Then, in 2020, Narges was forcibly moved to another prison. All her documents were gone. And she had to start all over.".

But she managed to rewrite it all, and her texts were smuggled out of prison in fragments by fellow prisoners and visitors who risked their own safety.

In her memoir, Mohammadi recounts pivotal moments in her life, including her childhood and youth, how she started taking action against gender discrimination, political repression, the death penalty and human rights abuses, and the personal and emotional toll of her activism.

In a recent development, the human rights activist has been sentenced to a combined total of more than 44 years in prison and 154 lashes. For more than a decade, she has been separated from her twin children, who are now 19 years old and live in exile in France for their own protection.

Born on April 21, 1972, in Zanjan, Iran, Narges Mohammadi became politically active while studying in physics at Imam Khomeini University of Qazvin in the 1990s.

In "A Woman Never Stops Fighting," she describes how she started mountain climbing as a student, and organized mixed-gender groups dedicated to mountaineering — a controversial initiative at the time. She also helped establish an independent student organization and advocated for political reform. Her activities led to repeated harassment and arrests by authorities.

It has been revealed that she began her journalism career in 1996, writing about Iran's student and women's movements. As her public profile grew, she became increasingly involved in Iran's civil society and human rights community.

It has been revealed that in 1998, she married political activist Taghi Rahmani. The couple's twins, Ali and Kiana, were born in 2006.

Over the course of her career, Mohammadi worked with some of Iran's most prominent human rights organizations and became a leading figure in the Defenders of Human Rights Centre, founded by 2003 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Shirin Ebadi.

In a recent development, she played a key role in initiatives promoting free elections, peace and the abolition of the death penalty, especially for juvenile offenders. She also helped establish organizations supporting political prisoners and advocating for women's rights.

Her first major prison sentence related to her human rights activities came in 2011. It marked the beginning of a cycle of arrests and prosecutions that would define much of her adult life.

Sources indicate that in her memoir, she describes an arrest that took place in front of her young children. At one point during her imprisonment, she lost the right to call them for several months.

She also details the brutal treatment she experienced in prison, with constant interrogations, beatings and denial of medical care.

Another central focus of her activism is denouncing the psychological effects of solitary confinement, which she had previously documented with fellow inmates in her book and documentary project "White Torture.".

It has been revealed that "When someone is subjected to physical torture, the scars, blood and infections — dreadful as they may be — serve as visible witnesses," she writes in her memoir. But, she adds, "when someone is subjected to psychological torture, no visible traces remain, and the victim cannot justify the trauma — neither to themselves nor to others. In fact, it becomes virtually impossible to even accept that one has been tortured at all, which causes the suffering to continue indefinitely.".

"This is also the goal of solitary confinement: to bring the imprisoned person to the very edge of nothingness — to strip them of their identity and of everything that makes them human," she writes.

Through her relentless campaigning against executions and state violence, she helped bring these concerns to the forefront of public debate among Iranian activists.

International recognition of her work culminated in October 2023 when she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "for her fight against the oppression of women in Iran and her fight to promote human rights and freedom for all.".

As Mohammadi was unable to attend the ceremony because she remained imprisoned in Tehran's Evin Prison, the award was accepted on her behalf by her teenage twins, who delivered her message to the world.

Following the Nobel Prize, Iranian authorities continued to pursue upcoming legal cases against her, restrict her communications and intensify pressure on her from prison.

She became the target of a systematic smear campaign, including widespread defamation, gender-based harassment and explicit death threats.

Sources indicate that "We are firmly convinced that the Islamic Republic of Iran has deployed its cyber army — which is the second-largest, after Russia's — to this end," states Claren of the Narges Mohammadi Foundation. Conspiracy theorists even started claiming she might be working for the regime, she adds: "And what is truly terrible about this is that when a lie is repeated over and over again and spread over the course of years, it eventually leads even ordinary people to start believing it.".

Recent findings suggest that in late 2024, following surgery, Mohammadi was granted a temporary medical release. Doctors warned at the time that a return to prison could seriously endanger her health.

Nevertheless, Mohammadi was brutally arrested again in December 2025, while attending a memorial ceremony for Khosrow Alikordi, a lawyer and human rights activist who died in suspicious circumstances.

In a recent development, in prison, she was held in solitary confinement for an extended period and her health continued to deteriorate, Claren reports. But "thanks to a public campaign, she has now been granted what is known as an interruption of detention for medical reasons.".

But "that doesn't mean she is free," adds Claren, who notes that she still suffers from serious health problems — as do many Iranians who have been tortured in prison.

In February, an Iranian court ordered additional prison sentences for Mohammadi, along with a travel ban.

It has been revealed that mohammadi lives in constant fear of having to return to prison any day, notes Claren, and "this all comes with the pressure to which Iranian civil society — including, of course, people like Narges — is currently subjected, with questions like: Will Trump launch an attack, yes or no? Will there be another war?".

Despite this uncertainty, Mohammadi continues her activism. Her international profile also helps her supporters keep addressing publicly the issue of human rights in Iran in the public eye, indicates Claren: "It is incredibly important that, alongside the individual Narges Mohammadi, the focus also remains consistently on the struggle of the people in Iran for freedom, dignity, and fundamental rights — for the right to sing and dance.".

Tech Report: Sore throat? The brain has surprising control over how ill you feel
